subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Concurrency follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Performance SLOs & Concurrency — follow-up and next steps

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and action items so we’re aligned: 

What we heard from ACME:
- Target user-facing SLO: p95 latency <= 150ms for text generation up to ~512 tokens (mostly streaming responses).
- Average request size: ~180 tokens; peak request size up to 2k tokens for some batch jobs.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~500 requests/sec during business hours; burst to ~1,200 req/s for short windows.
- Concurrency: app needs ~200 concurrent streaming connections at peak; across services we may see up to 800 parallel in-flight requests during flash events.
- Connection model: long-lived HTTP/2 or WebSocket streaming (keep-alive), client-side pooling with up to 50 pooled connections per app node.

Questions we asked (and next steps):
1) Confirm which endpoints will use streaming vs non-streaming (you mentioned chat + multimodal previews will stream).
2) Provide a short sample of request size distribution (we asked for the matrix you promised).
3) Confirm whether you need strict per-client concurrency guarantees (e.g., 200 concurrent connections per customer tenant) or aggregate account-level concurrency.

Redwood action items:
- I’ll loop in Vivek to validate concurrency & streaming requirements against our rate limit model and propose an initial quota + burst profile.
- We’ll provide an example rate-limit config and an appendix explaining connection pooling best practices for HTTP/2.
- Send a draft Mutual Action Plan and a quote reflecting either hosted usage or a Dedicated capacity recommendation based on your concurrency SLOs.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short template (mutual-action-plan.docx) and a blank performance matrix for your team to fill (acme-performance-matrix.xlsx).

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Can you confirm the distribution (approx %) between streaming vs non-streaming traffic?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Streaming vs non-streaming split: ~70% streaming (user chat previews & live suggestions), ~30% short non-streaming inference (background ranking).
- Request distribution: 60% small requests (~64-256 tokens), 30% medium (256-512), 10% large (>512). I’ll attach the CSV/matrix by EOD.
- Concurrency nuance: we need two guarantees — (1) per-tenant peak concurrency for our largest customers ~200 concurrent streams each (these are high-value customers), and (2) aggregate account concurrency target of ~800 concurrent in-flight requests across all tenants.
- Pooling: our frontend runs 20 nodes; we plan connection pools of 30-50 connections/node. We want guidance on optimal keep-alive and whether HTTP/2 multiplexing is preferred for stable latency.

One ask: given the per-tenant concurrency requirement, can Redwood provide a suggested quota model (per-tenant concurrency limit + account-level burst) and what the incremental cost looks like for sustained 800-concurrency vs Dedicated capacity?

I’m attaching the performance matrix (acme-performance-matrix.xlsx).

Best,
Sophie Turner
Head of Product — Conversational AI, ACME Corp
sophie.turner@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Concurrency — follow-up and next steps

Sophie — thanks for the matrix, looks great. High-level responses below; Vivek and Rishi are cc’d to add technical / pricing granularity.

1) Quota model we recommend:
- Per-tenant concurrency reserve: configure a guaranteed concurrency bucket (e.g., 200 concurrent tokens/streams) per VIP tenant. This prevents noisy neighbors from impacting your largest customers.
- Account-level burst: allow an aggregate burst pool (e.g., 1,000 concurrent requests) for flash events with token-based billing for overage.
- Rate limits: we typically enforce a per-connection QPS and per-account token rate at the control plane; for streaming connections we also track concurrent open streams.

2) Hosted vs Dedicated guidance:
- Hosted API: we can raise hosted rate limits and configure per-tenant concurrency; however, sustained 800+ concurrent in-flight requests with p95 <150ms across 512 tokens will be in a higher usage tier and could be cost-inefficient at scale. We can offer a committed monthly usage block + elevated burst pools for hosted.
- Dedicated: for predictable SLOs at that scale, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) is typically recommended. It gives predictable throughput, isolation, and the ability to fine-tune kernel/runtime settings for streaming.

3) Connection pooling & HTTP/2:
- HTTP/2 multiplexing + long-lived connections is recommended for streaming. Keep-alive of ~5 minutes is reasonable.
- Advise 20-40 pools per node with per-connection concurrency limits to avoid head-of-line in client-side queues.

Vivek, can you validate these numbers against our typical GPU throughput assumptions and propose: (a) an initial hosted quota profile (per-tenant concurrency + aggregate burst) and (b) a rough Dedicated configuration (number of GPU slices/nodes) that would meet 800 sustained concurrency with p95 target?

Rishi — please include a pricing delta (hosted elevated tier vs Dedicated baseline) and any minimum commit terms. I'll assemble a draft MAP after we have your inputs.

Thanks — 
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:24:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Concurrency — follow-up and next steps

Hi all — quick validation from infra/runtime side.

Numbers & assumptions:
- p95 <=150ms for ~512 tokens (streaming): on our optimized runtime this is achievable with ~8-12 tokens/ms sampling depending on model family; primary lever is batching and KV-cache reuse.
- For ACME's distribution, to sustain 800 concurrent in-flight requests (70% streaming) with p95 target, approximate Dedicated recommendation: 8 x A100-class GPU slices (or equivalent) with smart sharding and continuous batching. This assumes efficient streaming/hybrid batching.
- Hosted quota profile (initial conservative):
  * Per-tenant concurrency reserve: 200 concurrent streaming connections (guaranteed)
  * Account aggregate burst pool: 1,000 concurrent streams for short bursts (60-120s)
  * Sustained hosted soft-limit: 500 concurrent streams (billing + throttle beyond)

Operational notes:
- We can configure token-based overage billing and temporary elevated burst windows (DocuSign link for approval + we’ll need an accepted MAP).
- For HTTP/2 keep-alives, 3-5 minutes is fine; encourage client-side backpressure (max inflight per connection) to keep latency tight.
- We’ll instrument per-tenant metrics (concurrency, p95 latency, token usage) and expose them in Redwood Console so ACME can set alerts.

Next steps:
- Rishi to propose pricing delta for hosted elevated tier vs Dedicated monthly commit.
- Marissa to send MAP + draft quote.
- Sophie to confirm whether you want Redwood to manage per-tenant concurrency enforcement or if ACME will reflect limits in the client.

-Vivek
